newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Sing dollar catches up on weakness.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Sing dollar catches up on weakness.

text.p: * The Singapore dollar weakens sharply against the greenback after crashing through pyschological support at 1.4500 to
touch a low of 1.4535.
* The Malaysian ringgit continues to look weak against the
dollar after touching low of 2.5930 in holiday thinned trade.
* Thai baht softens slightly, but the dollar is seen capped at around 30.50/31.00 as some forwards mature.
* Indonesian rupiah steady in quiet trade with Jakarta
on holdiay. Some unwinding of dollar positions as speculators lie low.
* Philippine peso steady at open with the central bank
coming in to sell dollars at 29 in the morning.
The Singapore dollar looks set to touch new year lows against the greenback after it crashed through support of 1.4500 in early Thursday trade, dealers said.
The Sing revisted its year low touched in March of 1.4535 on stop loss sales by hedge funds after it broke the 1.4500 level, they said.
"The Sing is just weakening on the back of the slide in the ringgit and the rupiah," said a regional currencies dealer at a European bank.

"It is basically playing a catch up game with the other regional currencies. If you look at the ringgit, it has weakened almost five percent against the dollar in the last week and the Sing has not really moved," he said.

Dealers said it was hard to see where the Sing would see support but they said the absence from the market of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), the de facto central bank, was likely to encourage furthher slides.
The Sing was expected to trade within a new range of 1.4480 to 1.4550 in the near term, said one dealer.
Another dealer said the Sing's weakness was likely to continue as "under-hedged" corporations were likely to buy more dollars.
Trading in the Malaysian ringgit and the Indonesian rupiah was thin with the forex markets in the two countries closed for a Moslem regligious holiday.
The ringgit, however, continued to look weak against the U.S. dollar, dealers in Singapore said.
The ringgit was sold overnight by London parties despite Bank Negara checking rates at around 2.4700.

"There is very little business being done today as the spread is very wide about 30-50 points," said a Singapore-based dealer. He said the ringgit was expected to range between 2.5860 to 2.5930 for the day.
The Indonesian rupiah was also quiet, moving within a range of 2,470 to 2,480, but there was some selling of dollars seen, said Singapore dealers.

Traders had bought dollars ahead of the holiday in aniticipation of a possible attack on the rupiah. "But nothing is happening today, so it is a case of sell the rupiah on rumours and buy on facts," one dealer said.
He said the rupiah was likely to stay within 2,470 to 2,490 for the rest of the day.
The Thai baht eased against the dollar in early morning trade on high dollar demand by importers and the U.S. unit's rise abroad, dealers in Bangkok said.
The baht was quoted at 30.08/30.15 per dollar early onshore against 29.95/30.00 late on Wednesday.
The central bank said the weighted average interbank exchange rate was 30.062 per dollar against 29.967 on Wednesday.
Dealers in Singapore said the dollar was likely be capped at around 30.50/31.00 offshore as there was demand for baht funds with some maturities in forwards due.
"There is some dollar selling this morning because of the maturities. We think the dollar/baht will be capped at around the 30 figure for a while," said a Singapore dealer.
The Philippine peso was higher at 29.26 in early trade against its Wednesday close of 29.30, but trading was light, dealers in the Philippines said.
They said the central bank had come in to support the peso by selling dollars at 29.00. The bank has been selling dollars since it decided last Friday to let the peso move in a wider range.
-- Anchalee Koetsawang in Bangkok (662) 652-0642, Lilian
